deep_dive.title: LIFT: Local Metric Alignment and Foundation-guided Propagation for Few-shot Depth Completion
deep_dive.abstract: Few-shot depth completion aims to recover dense metric depth from sparse measurements using only a small number of target-domain annotations, offering a favorable balance between annotation cost and model adaptation. We propose LIFT, a framework that harnesses both depth and feature priors from a frozen pretrained monocular depth estimation (MDE) foundation model for few-shot depth completion. Specifically, LIFT first estimates local scale and shift parameters on a coarse grid and interpolates them into smooth, dense parameter fields, providing a spatially adaptive metric depth initialization. It then progressively refines this initialization through multi-scale depth propagation guided by foundation features. Finally, a lightweight residual decoder combines multi-level foundation features with propagation correction to refine the metric depth. Extensive experiments on NYUv2 and KITTI-DC demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance. The source code will soon be released.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对少样本深度补全中标注昂贵、跨域适配困难的问题，本文提出LIFT框架，复用冻结的预训练单目深度估计基础模型所提供的深度与特征先验。方法先在粗网格上估计局部尺度与平移参数并插值为稠密参数场，得到空间自适应的度量深度初值，再借助基础模型特征进行多尺度深度传播细化。实验表明该框架在少量目标域标注下即可恢复稠密且准确的度量深度，兼顾标注成本与模型适配性，为深度基础模型的下游复用提供了可行路径。

deep_dive.title: LangDepth: Vision-Language Scene Priors for Semantic Binning and Cross-Domain Monocular Depth Estimation
deep_dive.abstract: Monocular depth estimation has advanced through large-scale pretraining and strong visual backbones, yet metric depth remains sensitive to scene-level scale. Indoor rooms and outdoor driving scenes occupy very different depth ranges, but most depth decoders infer this global structure implicitly from visual features. We ask whether scene-level semantic structure can instead act as an upstream prior that shapes the metric output space before dense prediction.   We present LangDepth (SemanticBins), a monocular depth architecture that couples strong visual features with a scene-conditioned output space. A frozen CLIP encoder and a learnable bank of scene- and geometry-oriented concept keys convert image features into a compact scene descriptor, without requiring per-image text or an external captioner. A Scene Prior Module (SPM) maps this descriptor to a scene-conditioned metric depth interval, providing a global range anchor before dense decoding. In parallel, a DINOv2-L backbone with a lightweight FPN extracts dense visual features, and a Per-Pixel Assignment Network (PPAN) assigns pixels to the scene-prescribed bin structure. A confidence gate fuses the dense visual estimate with the SPM prior.   We train LangDepth jointly on NYU Depth V2 and KITTI under a modest supervised depth budget, without web-scale depth supervision or pseudo-labelled depth data. A single model achieves delta_1 = 0.960 on NYU, 0.960 on KITTI, 0.887 on DIODE indoor, 0.946 on iBims-1, and 0.861 on SUN RGB-D. Beyond aggregate accuracy, the SPM predicts compact indoor ranges and much wider outdoor KITTI ranges, the gate becomes SPM-dominant on outdoor scenes, and perturbing the routed scene context causes large drops on KITTI and iBims-1. These results support scene-conditioned output spaces as a practical and interpretable mechanism for cross-domain monocular depth estimation.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 单目深度估计虽受益于大规模预训练，但度量尺度对场景类型高度敏感，室内与车载场景深度范围差异巨大。作者提出 LangDepth，用冻结的 CLIP 编码器与可学习的场景/几何概念键，将图像特征转换为场景条件化的深度输出空间，先确定全局尺度再做稠密预测。实验表明该方法在跨域场景下提升了度量深度精度与泛化性，说明把场景级语义作为上游先验可有效约束尺度歧义。

quick_skim.title: BiRefNet-V2: Rethinking Bilateral Reference for High-Resolution Dichotomous Image Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Dichotomous image segmentation requires pixel-accurate foreground-background separation while preserving fine structures such as thin filaments, sharp edges, and intricate textures. BiRefNet addressed this challenge through bilateral references, combining image patches and gradient information, but its inward reference loses local spatial structure and lacks semantic guidance, while its outward reference relies on single-channel gradient attention. We recast this paradigm as controlled information recovery - locality determines what spatial information survives, semantic selectivity what information enters, and focused boundary supervision where refinement occurs - and propose BiRefNet-V2 to implement it: (1) locality-preserving and semantically guided detail injection through space-to-depth transformation, overlapping patches, and a Semantically Guided Gate; (2) a learned boundary stream with focused supervision that generates full-channel residual attention without requiring boundary annotations; and (3) a dual-branch decoder integrating depth-wise boundary convolutions with large-kernel attention. A modernized framework - LayerNorm, GELU, the Lion optimizer, and a DINOv3 backbone - cuts training from 600 to 50 epochs. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on DIS5K, camouflaged object detection, and high-resolution salient object detection across all 13 evaluation sets. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet-V2.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对高分辨率二分图像分割中细丝、锐边与复杂纹理难以保真的问题，本文指出原双边参考的向内分支丢失局部空间结构、向外分支仅依赖单通道梯度注意力。作者将范式重构为可控信息恢复，通过保局部性的图像块参考、语义选择与聚焦边界监督实现像素级前景背景分离。实验显示该方法在精细结构与边界处取得更高精度，为高分辨率前景提取提供了通用框架。
